title: Clinical and radiologic characterization of rare head and neck tumors
summary: Some tumors of the head and neck region are very rare. Because only few people are affected, little is known so far about how best to detect and treat these tumors and which factors influence the course of the disease. In this study, we retrospectively review existing medical records, imaging examinations and findings of patients who were treated for a rare head and neck tumor at the Medical Center – University of Freiburg since 2007. We aim to understand how the disease develops, which treatments were given and which features are linked to a more favorable or less favorable course. The results should help to detect such tumors earlier in the future and to improve diagnosis, treatment and aftercare for affected patients. Only existing data are used; no additional examinations and no contact with patients take place.
conditions: Rare head and neck tumors, including sarcomas, sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinomas, basaloid squamous cell carcinomas, malignant skin tumors of the external auditory canal, mucosal malignant melanomas, paragangliomas and salivary gland carcinomas, as well as head and neck tumors discussed in the molecular tumor board.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically confirmed rare head and neck tumor (e.g. sarcoma, sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma, basaloid squamous cell carcinoma, malignant skin tumor of the external auditory canal, mucosal malignant melanoma, paraganglioma, salivary gland carcinoma) or presentation of a head and neck tumor at the molecular tumor board
- First diagnosis and/or treatment at the Medical Center – University of Freiburg from 01 January 2007 onwards
- Adequate documentation of baseline parameters (at least date of diagnosis, tumor site, histological diagnosis, and TNM stage or comparable staging)
Exclusion criteria:
- Absence of essential baseline data (e.g. no confirmed histological diagnosis or no information on tumor site)
- Objection by the patient to the use of their health data for research purposes
